programmes.name: ECMWF — AIFS ENS (Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System, ensemble)
programmes.step: Selecting the ensemble size for AIFS ENS and generating its members. The card targets the operational decision to run 51 members (50 perturbed + 1 control), asking whether scaling to 1,000 members sharpens top-percentile wind/temperature/rain probability forecasts or whether the members — exchangeable draws of one afCRPS-trained distribution — share enough model error that the tail stops sharpening.
programmes.step_quote: AIFS ENS currently has 50 perturbed members and one control member. However, unlike the physics-based IFS ENS, where the control member uses unperturbed initial conditions and the forecast model is unperturbed as well, the AIFS ENS control member also starts from unperturbed initial conditions but still includes model-generated variations during the forecast. This means that all AIFS ENS members, including the control, are stochastic forecasts that represent different outcomes from a learned forecast distribution.

activity.claim: AIFS ENS v1 became operational on 1 July 2025 and was superseded by AIFS ENS v2, implemented on 12 May 2026; the AIFS-CRPS paper was published in npj Artificial Intelligence on 2 February 2026.
activity.quote: AIFS ENS v2 was successfully implemented on 12 May 2026, 06 UTC run.

practice.claim: Operational scale: a 51-member (50 perturbed + 1 control), 15-day, 6-hourly global forecast run four times per day at ~0.25° (N320, ~31 km).
practice.quote: It is run operationally by ECMWF, generating a 51-member 15-day (6-hourly) global forecast four times per day.

practice.claim: Members are generated by injecting noise into the processor, so any number of members can be drawn from one trained model; only two members are used in training.
practice.quote: When generating forecasts, as many members as required can be generated by providing different random seeds to the model. Two ensemble members are used in training.

practice.claim: The model is trained with the almost-fair CRPS (afCRPS) and produces exchangeable members of a single learned distribution — the exact setup whose shared model error the card's 'if not' branch suspects of capping tail sharpness.
practice.quote: The trained model is stochastic and can generate as many exchangeable members as desired.

practice.claim: Tooling: implemented with the open-source Anemoi framework, with weights and a demo notebook released on Hugging Face so the community can run AIFS ENS themselves.
practice.quote: AIFS ENS v2 is implemented using the Anemoi framework. Anemoi consists of open source components, enabling the user community to run AIFS themselves.

practice.claim: People: developed at ECMWF by Simon Lang, Linus Magnusson, Mihai Alexe, Mariana Clare, Christopher Roberts, Matthew Chantry and colleagues.
practice.quote: Lang, Simon, Alexe, Mihai, Clare, Mariana C. A., Roberts, Christopher, Adewoyin, Rilwan

programmes.if_lever_changes: If skill keeps rising past 50 members (1,000 members sharpen top-percentile tails), ECMWF would gain concrete evidence to justify raising the operational AIFS ENS size above 51 members, or running on-demand large-member forecasts for high-impact events, improving its extreme wind/temperature/rain probability products.
programmes.if_not_changes: If skill flattens near 50 members, ECMWF's current 51-member operational configuration is confirmed as sufficient — shared model error from a single afCRPS-trained distribution caps tail sharpness, so extra members waste compute and effort should instead go to improving the model itself (e.g., the multi-scale loss and physical bounds already introduced in v2).

already_done.claim: ECMWF has studied ensemble-size sensitivity and fair scores for its physics-based IFS ensemble up to 200 members (and this fair-score theory underlies afCRPS), but it has not published a 1,000-member AIFS-ENS top-percentile extreme-scoring experiment — operationally it still runs 51 members.
already_done.quote: The sensitivity of forecast quality to ensemble size varies depending on which verification metrics are considered. ... For a score that measures the skill of quantiles in the tail of the distribution, the sensitivity to ensemble size is considerably larger.

programmes.name: HENS (Huge Ensembles) — LBNL × NVIDIA × NERSC
programmes.step: Generating a huge ML ensemble and scoring how well it samples the tails of the forecast distribution for extreme events. The card re-runs this exact ensemble-size-to-extreme-skill question, but for AIFS-ENS (exchangeable draws of one afCRPS-trained distribution) instead of HENS's SFNO-BVMC (which explicitly adds model uncertainty via 29 independently-trained checkpoints).
programmes.step_quote: we generate a huge ensemble (HENS), with 7424 members initialized each day of summer 2023. We enumerate the technical requirements for running huge ensembles at this scale. HENS precisely samples the tails of the forecast distribution and presents a detailed sampling of internal variability.

activity.claim: HENS Part 2 was published in Geoscientific Model Development on 4 September 2025, and the HENS method continues to be maintained and shipped as the 'HENS recipe' inside NVIDIA's actively-developed earth2studio (v0.19.0 on 30 September 2026, commits through 12 October 2026); the original LBNL earth2mip/modulus-makani forks serve as the archived reference implementation.

practice.claim: Scale: 7,424 members = 29 independently-trained SFNO checkpoints × 256 bred-vector initial-condition perturbations, each run 15 days for 92 summer-2023 initial dates.
practice.quote: Here, we combine these two perturbation techniques to create a 7424-member ensemble: 256 initial condition perturbations for each of the 29 SFNO checkpoints.

practice.claim: Compute: generated on 256 NVIDIA A100 80 GB GPUs at NERSC's Perlmutter supercomputer — ~45 minutes and 21 TB per initial date, 18,432 GPU-hours total, ~2 PB of saved fields.
practice.quote: Generating the ensemble for each initial date requires 21 TB of space and 45 min using 256 80 GB NVIDIA A100 GPUs.

practice.claim: Tools: NVIDIA's earth2mip for inference/scoring/analysis and modulus-makani for training; people span LBNL (Ankur Mahesh, William Collins, Mark Risser, Shashank Subramanian), NVIDIA (Boris Bonev, Noah Brenowitz, Yair Cohen, Karthik Kashinath, Thorsten Kurth) and NERSC.
practice.quote: There are two primary codebases for HENS: modulus-makani (used for training the ML models) and earth2mip (used for inference, scoring, and analysis).

practice.claim: HENS's headline extreme-scaling finding, which the card directly probes: larger ensembles systematically improve extreme-event metrics.
practice.quote: HENS reduces the RMSE of the best ensemble member; with larger ensembles, this metric systematically decreases by up to 50 % (Fig. 7).

programmes.if_lever_changes: If AIFS-ENS keeps gaining past 50 members, HENS's central thesis — huge ensembles buy better forecasts of rare extremes — extends to single-distribution CRPS ensembles that lack HENS's 29-checkpoint model perturbation, strengthening the case that member count alone is the lever and that operational centres should adopt large ML ensembles for extreme-event probability forecasting.
programmes.if_not_changes: If AIFS-ENS saturates near 50 members, it would show HENS's tail-sampling gains came at least partly from its explicit multi-checkpoint model uncertainty rather than member count alone — implying exchangeable single-distribution members cannot substitute for model perturbation, and future huge-ensemble work must retain multiple independently-trained models to keep improving extremes.

already_done.claim: HENS already ran the analogous huge-ensemble extreme-scoring experiment and quantified ensemble-size benefit — but with SFNO-BVMC (29 checkpoints + bred vectors), not AIFS-ENS; the specific question of whether exchangeable draws of one afCRPS-trained distribution saturate from shared model error is untested.
already_done.quote: Figure 2 shows the information gain as a function of ensemble size. The 7424-member ensemble has an information gain of 4.

programmes.name: NVIDIA Earth-2 (earth2studio)
programmes.step: Running and verifying ML ensemble forecasts — including ECMWF's AIFS ENS — at scale in an open framework. The card's workflow (run AIFS-ENS with 10–1,000 members, score top-percentile extremes with fair CRPS and Brier) maps directly onto earth2studio's ensemble model wrappers and its verification/scoring tooling.
programmes.step_quote: Added ECMWF AIFSENS ensemble prognostic model wrapper

activity.claim: earth2studio ships releases roughly monthly (v0.19.0 on 30 September 2026) and had commits through 12 October 2026.

practice.claim: earth2studio already wraps and runs ECMWF's AIFS ENS v1 ('AIFSENS' wrapper, v0.11.0) and AIFS ENS v2 with stochastic noise injection ('AIFS2ENS', v0.16.0), and ships AIFS_ENS forecast data sources (v0.10.0) — so a 1,000-member AIFS-ENS extreme run is directly buildable on its stack.
practice.quote: Added AIFS 2.0 ensemble prognostic model (AIFS2ENS) with stochastic noise injection

practice.claim: It provides the exact ensemble verification metrics the card uses, including Brier score and fair CRPS.
It maintains the HENS huge-ensemble pipeline as a first-party recipe, with multi-checkpoint inference, CorrDiff downscaling and tropical-cyclone tracking bolted on.
practice.quote: This project implements a multi-checkpoint inference pipeline for large-scale ensemble weather forecasting.

practice.claim: People: maintained by the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo Team, distributed under Apache-2.0.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If 1,000 AIFS-ENS members keep improving extremes, NVIDIA Earth-2 gains a validated, near-free recipe for rare-extreme probability forecasting on top of the AIFS-ENS wrappers it already ships — e.g., a 'huge AIFS-ENS ensemble for extremes' workflow plus ensemble-size-scaling guidance in earth2studio's scorecards.
programmes.if_not_changes: If skill saturates near 50 members, Earth-2's guidance would instead document that scaling members on a single CRPS-trained distribution has diminishing returns, steering users toward multi-model/multi-checkpoint (HENS-style) ensembles rather than raw member inflation and deprioritizing 1,000-member AIFS-ENS runs.

already_done.claim: earth2studio provides the AIFS-ENS wrappers and Brier/fair-CRPS metrics to run this experiment, but it has not published (and its scorecards do not yet cover) a 1,000-member AIFS-ENS top-percentile extreme-scoring study across the 10–1,000-member axis.
already_done.quote: New metrics: Brier score, fractions skill score, log spectral distance, mean absolute error

gaps: Unknown whether ECMWF has run unpublished internal >51-member AIFS-ENS experiments for extremes; only the 51-member operational configuration and the physics-based IFS ensemble-size studies (<=200 members) are public.

The exact latest commit date of the HENS recipe folder inside NVIDIA/earth2studio was not captured; activity is inferred from earth2studio's overall v0.19.0 release (30 Sep 2026) and commits through 12 Oct 2026.

Google DeepMind's GenCast/FGN (and physics-based huge-ensemble efforts such as UNSEEN) were not included because they do not run AIFS-ENS, so they would not directly consume an AIFS-ENS-specific ensemble-size result.
